name: GHRP-4
lead: GHRP-4 is a synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide in the numbered GHRP series, alongside GHRP-1, -2, -5, -6, hexarelin, ipamorelin and alexamorelin. Analytical papers describe the family as synthetic met-enkephalin analogues containing unnatural D-amino acids, designed to stimulate growth hormone release.[1] The chain that interest in this class rests on is more growth hormone secretion, then higher IGF-1 signalling, then support for lean mass, recovery and fat loss, the outcomes bodybuilding and physique communities care about.[2][4]

The GHRPs are described as orally active in animal work and as able to raise endogenous growth hormone production.[2] Most were never approved as drugs, and with the exception of GHRP-2 the group represents non-approved pharmaceuticals, yet are reported to be readily available through internet providers.[5]

GHRP-4 appears in the literature almost solely in anti-doping research, where laboratories have developed urine tests, metabolism studies and stability studies for it. No human clinical studies of GHRP-4 itself were found; human data exist for other peptides of the class.

paras: Growth hormone secretagogues act on the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR), and the Wikipedia overview lists GHRP-4 as a GHSR agonist without further detail.[4] Papers on peptide metabolism report that doping laboratories have studied how GHRPs are broken down so that their use can be detected; a 2012 study used oral and intravenous administration in rats, plus human serum and recombinant amidase experiments, because the metabolism of most GHRPs was largely unknown, with only one metabolite established for GHRP-2.[5]

In 2023, researchers synthesised GHRP-4, GHRP-5, GHRP-6 and sermorelin fragments by solid-phase synthesis and tested their stability against human blood, trypsin and chymotrypsin. They reported that GHRP-4, GHRP-6 and sermorelin (22-29) were stable to enzyme and blood treatment, which led the authors to propose them as in-house internal standards for quantifying peptides in biological samples.[6]

Because the established test for exogenous growth hormone does not detect secretagogue use, laboratories developed urine-based mass spectrometry screens for GHRPs including GHRP-4, in both human and equine samples.[2][1] A 2011 method extracted eight GHRPs including GHRP-4 from human urine for liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry detection,[2] and a 2014 validated screen was developed for use in horse racing and human athletics, with all eight GHRPs or their metabolites detectable in rat urine after intravenous administration.[1]

A 2016 screening paper using direct urine injection and ion-mobility mass spectrometry lists GHRP-4 among peptides prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency, with detection limits of 50 to 500 pg/mL against a minimum required performance level of 2 ng/mL.[3] The 2012 metabolism paper notes that new performance-enhancing compounds are rapidly distributed through internet platforms.[5]

No studies found of GHRP-4 in humans. Related human work concerns other peptides of the class: in a 1993 study, eight young men received a 24-hour infusion of the hexapeptide GHRP SK&F 110679, which increased GH secretion rates about eightfold compared with saline while GH release stayed pulsatile, and attenuated the response to a later GHRP bolus.[7] This study did not test GHRP-4.

card.summary: An obscure GH-releasing peptide that shows up in anti-doping papers and nowhere in human trials.
card.note: Prohibited in competitive sport; no human clinical studies found.

quick.overview:
GHRP-4 belongs to a family of synthetic peptides designed to prompt growth hormone release, and is discussed in muscle-building contexts.

The published record consists of doping-control chemistry. No human clinical studies were found.
quick.mechanism: It is classed as an agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor and is described as a met-enkephalin analogue.
quick.risks: No human safety data were found. It appears on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list and is not an approved medicine.

chain: Acts on the ghrelin/GH secretagogue receptor
Higher GH and IGF-1 signalling (claimed for the class)
Support for lean mass, recovery and leanness
angle.text: GHRPs are discussed in physique communities as GH-releasing peptides that could support lean mass and fat loss. For GHRP-4 specifically the published record is analytical chemistry from doping-control laboratories rather than human outcome studies.
